_readme: Events that happen during a stage. Each event has a stage, a station (a place on the ship) and facts written as { "value": ..., "source": ... }. A source is a link, a written game-design choice, or the word PLACEHOLDER (made up for now; a student replaces it before the final submission). The Mars shadow pass is NOT here: it is a Mars-orbit event and lives in game_data.json (events, power_low). The words on the screen are in data/inner_voice.json (flight) and data/story.json (flight). The science passes (stage arrival) are also here: three passes, each with a capture window and a downlink window in seconds, plus storage and downlink hours. The antenna speed and the camera data come from the parts. FLIGHT (batch 9): the Flight plan and its three events (water leak, air leak, food spoils) are in flight_plan, water_leak, air_leak and food_spoil. drain_per_second = how much of the supply an event pours out every real second.

station.source: Game-design choice: the Water station in the Life Support room (A10).

start_after_seconds.source: PLACEHOLDER (seconds after the Flight leg starts)

fix.source: Game-design choice: press E at the Water station.

drain_per_second.source: PLACEHOLDER (liters of water lost every real second until the leak is fixed; a leak fixed within about 30 s of the warning leaves the water out of the red)

passes.source: PLACEHOLDER (seconds after the Arrival walk starts; three science passes as in GAME_PLAN.md section 7: each pass is a capture window, then a downlink window). No two windows overlap. Between a window in one room and the next window in the other room there are at least 6 s, and the real walk speed is 4 m/s (player.gd) over about 16 m between the Science bay and the Comms room (4 s). Two passes come before the shadow pass (20 to 40 s) and one after it, and the mission clock ends at 60 s. A student can move them.

capture_days_worth.source: PLACEHOLDER (how many days of the camera's data one picture holds, in Gb per day times this)

storage_gb.source: PLACEHOLDER (a fixed onboard storage size in Gb; a student looks up the real recorder size)

downlink_hours.source: PLACEHOLDER (hours the ground station is in view; a student looks up the real contact time)

result_show_seconds.source: PLACEHOLDER (how long the ring stays on screen after the press)

power_note.value: camera off = no capture, antenna off = nothing sent
power_note.source: Game rule: uses the Reroute Power switches

antenna_speed_note.value: Mb/s come from game_data.json parts > antenna > communications (real NASA numbers, sourced there)

surface_work._readme: The surface work (Stage 4, surface destinations): a walkable area, a surface clock, and one task: collect the sample with a timed press (E). max_days = the most days a surface stay can have. The parts decide the real number of days: days = the smallest of (max_days), (spare power / power_cost_per_day_w) and (how many days the crew supplies from Flight last, when each surface day uses supply_days_per_day days of food, water and air). seconds_per_day = real seconds for one surface day. Every day costs power_cost_per_day_w of spare power. Every try (Perfect, Good or Miss) costs attempt_power_cost_w (the drill). A Miss also loses miss_days_lost day (the lander is moved). The sample is sample_distance_m meters from the lander, plus the 'distance' percent from a bad landing. A broken solar panel (landing damage) makes solar power smaller by that percent. Success rules are in game_data.json arrival_goals. THREE TASKS (batch 9): 1 collect the sample, 2 run the instrument at the instrument station, 3 send the data home at the lander. All three must be done for MISSION SUCCESS, and at least planned_gb of data must get home. The instrument stores camera Gb per day x capture_days_worth x its press result factor x the surface tool's instrument_data_factor, never more than the computer's storage (storage_gb plus the computer's bonus). Sending home sends the least of what is stored and (the antenna's real speed x downlink_hours x the press result factor). instrument_power_cost_w and send_power_cost_w are used from the spare power, like the sample tries, and are kept back when the days are counted. instrument_distance_m = how far the instrument station is from the lander. days_needed = the fewest days the three tasks need (Review shows a red card below it). A build can give 0 days: nothing forces a day the power cannot pay for.

seconds_per_day.source: PLACEHOLDER (real seconds for one surface day; 15 s so that two days are enough to walk to every station)

power_cost_per_day_w.source: PLACEHOLDER (watts of spare power each surface day uses up)

attempt_power_cost_w.source: PLACEHOLDER (watts of spare power one sample try uses). Small numbers, so that even the default Small solar build gets at least 3 days at Jezero.

supply_days_per_day.source: PLACEHOLDER (one surface day uses this many days of the crew's food, water and air)

miss_days_lost.source: PLACEHOLDER (days lost after a missed sample try)

sample_distance_m.source: PLACEHOLDER (meters from the lander to the sample)

result_show_seconds.source: PLACEHOLDER (how long the ring stays on screen after the press)

end_read_seconds.source: PLACEHOLDER (seconds to read the last line before the report)

instrument_power_cost_w.source: PLACEHOLDER (watts of spare power the instrument run uses; small, see the sample try)

send_power_cost_w.source: PLACEHOLDER (watts of spare power sending the data home uses; small, see the sample try)

instrument_distance_m.source: PLACEHOLDER (meters from the lander to the instrument station)

planned_gb.source: PLACEHOLDER (the least data that must get home, in Gb: a small antenna can only just do it with a Perfect press, a large antenna always can; a student sets a goal from a real mission)

capture_days_worth.source: PLACEHOLDER (days of the camera's data one instrument run holds, in Gb per day times this)

storage_gb.source: PLACEHOLDER (onboard storage size in Gb, the same as the science pass)

downlink_hours.source: PLACEHOLDER (hours the ground station is in view)

days_needed.source: PLACEHOLDER (the fewest surface days the three tasks need: a build that gives fewer shows a red card on the Review screen)

flyby_pass._readme: The Europa flyby (Stage 4, flyby destinations): four timed presses with SPACE from mission control, then the pass. point_instrument and capture decide how much data is captured: captured = camera Gb per day x capture_days_worth x the point factor x the capture factor (never more than storage_gb). protect_computer decides the radiation loss: loss percent = radiation_loss_percent x (1 - the radiation shield's protection) x the press's loss factor. send_data sends min(what is stored, the antenna's real speed x downlink_hours x the press factor). planned_gb = the least data that must get home for MISSION SUCCESS. The radio delay is the real one from destinations.json.

planned_gb.source: PLACEHOLDER (a student sets a goal from a real mission)

capture_days_worth.source: PLACEHOLDER (days of the camera's data one flyby captures, in Gb per day times this)

storage_gb.source: PLACEHOLDER (same onboard storage size as the Mars science pass)

downlink_hours.source: PLACEHOLDER (hours the ground station listens to the data)

radiation_loss_percent.source: PLACEHOLDER (percent of the stored data a bad radiation hit destroys, with no shield). NASA: near Jupiter the Galileo orbiter faced '25 times more radiation than the level considered deadly for humans': https://science.nasa.gov/mission/galileo/

pass_seconds.source: PLACEHOLDER (real seconds the pass animation takes)

flight_plan._readme: The Flight plan (Stage 3). legs = the legs of the trip in order. Each leg has tasks (ids from the tasks list below; a task the ship cannot do, such as harvest without a garden, is left out) and one event (an id from this file: water_leak, air_leak or food_spoil). Every leg stands for trip_days divided by the number of legs (destinations.json) and lasts flight_leg_seconds. A trip with no crew plays no_crew_legs leg(s) and has no tasks or events. Each task has a station on the ship, the crew supply it looks after, and skip_loss_percent = how much of that meter's full size is lost at the end of the leg if the task was skipped (a skipped task makes its meter drop faster). A leak or spoil that is not fixed stops when the leg ends. Rationing is on for the rest of the trip once it is on.

no_crew_legs.source: Game-design choice (agent's choice for Kaleb, 2026-11-13): a trip with no crew has no crew supplies, so it has no tasks to play; it keeps one leg, as before.

legs.source: GAME_PLAN.md section 6b: 3 legs, each with 2-3 routine tasks and 1 event. Which task and event go in which leg is a game-design choice (agent's choice for Kaleb, 2026-11-13).

skip_loss_percent.source: Game-design choice: skipping the ration has no extra loss, because the crew simply eats the normal amount.

needs_part.source: Game rule: only a ship with a garden (life support part) can harvest.

days_per_fuel_percent.source: PLACEHOLDER (extra trip days for every percent of fuel lost at the launch: lost fuel means a slower trip, so the crew uses more supplies)
